GXO and Apptronik outline conditional rollout of up to 1,000 Apollos

GXO and Apptronik announced a letter of intent on November 12 to expand Apollo trials and develop a service framework. Subject to jointly agreed performance targets, they intend to deploy up to 1,000 robots over four years, starting in North America in late 2027. These are not delivered units or an unconditional purchase order.

Humanoids Daily ↗12 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

An intention, not an unconditional order

GXO and Apptronik announced a letter of intent on November 12 to expand Apollo trials and develop a service framework. Subject to jointly agreed performance targets, they intend to deploy up to 1,000 robots over four years, starting in North America in late 2027. These are not delivered units or an unconditional purchase order.

Testing warehouse workflows

Picking, case and tote movement, packing and sortation are in scope. The partners report collecting data and conducting autonomous evaluations on more than 50 tasks at Robot Park. Live operations will test productivity, safety and operational KPIs, including integration with employees and existing automation.

Commercial details remain open

The expected Robotics-as-a-Service framework has no disclosed pricing, named sites or Apollo generation. This is distinct from GXO’s Agility Digit expansion and Apollo’s Mercedes-Benz pilot. Results and commitments from those separate projects should not be treated as evidence that this rollout is already secured.
